full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 1.3.77 passed in Title Suit No. 70 of 1974 and the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 145 of 1951 and the sole-decree, in Rent Suit No. 22 of 1957 are null and void, in operation, without any basis, collusive and not binding on the plaintiff and for a further declaration that the suit land is an enemy property stating, inter alia, that the suit land measuring 1.18 decimals of land of Khatian No. 22, Mouza Sukani in which Sailabala had /8/ annas raiyati interest, Anupanm and Manupama Debi had -/8/- annas interest. The said recorded owners were in possession of the suit land in whose names the kahtian was finally prepared and published. The entire interest of Sailabala was transferred to the plaintiff by registered Kabala dated 29.2.1957 and handed over possession thereof wherein the plaintiff has been residing by constructing houses, planting trees. Anupama and Manupama Debi prior to their leaving this country handed over possession of their annas interest to the plaintiff and subsequently the same became enemy property. The plaintiff being co-sharer appalled for the same which was leased out to him on local enquiiy in Lease. 'Case Nos. 37 and 38 of 1967-68. The plaintiff on payment of the lease money became rightful possessor thereof and has been possessing the same by planting trees and rearing fish in the pond. .59 decimals out of 1.18 decimals were acquired by the Public Health Department and the rest .39 decimals is left with the plaintiff on the basis of said purchase and lease. The defendant no. 1 on certain false averments filed Title Suit No.70 of 1974 and obtained an ex pane decree taking the advantage of the absence of the plaintiff which was subsequently set aside on contest restoring the suit to its original file and number but upon a revision before the learned District Judge at the instance of the defendant no. 1, the revision was allowed maintaining the ex-parte decree. On a further .revision by the Government in this Court, the said order was maintained and as such the plaintiff could not take any step earlier for setting aside the ex-parte decree and the limitation can be over came by filing application under section 5 of the Limitation Act. Had the plaintiff been able to produce the evidence, the defendant No. 1 would not have been able to obtain the decree and as such prayed for declaring the said ex-parte decree dated 1.3.77 as null, void, in operative etc. Plaintiffs further case is that one Kartile Chandra Chattapaddya filed Rent Suit No. 22 of 1957 against the defendant No. 1 and obtained a sole-decree on the assertion that Anupama- and Manupama leased cut their land in favour of him and prayed for setting aside the said sole-decree which has not affected the interest of the plaintiff. The plaintiff further alleged that the defendant no. 1 has also disclosed about a decree in favour of defendant no. 1 in Title Suit No: 145 of 1951. There was no service of notice upon the defendants .of that suit and the decree was obtained by fraudulent suppression of summons/notice and has prayed for declaring the said decree as void, in operative etc/The plaintiff further alleged that since 1967 the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land by paying rent to the enemy property authority. The plaintiff further alleged that in the event of an auction dated 30.5.67 in Rent Execution Case No. -167 of 1956 the suit land was auction purchased by one Mominuddin Mollah and the plaintiff filed sale set aside Case No. 78. of 1957 under the provision of section 174 of the Bengal Tenancy 'Act and the same was. accordingly set aside and the plaintiff paid the rent due and has been possessing the suit land on payment of rent. As the suit land has been declared as enemy property the plaintiff obtained the pattan. The Amalnama of the defendant no. 1 is forged and antedated .and the plaintiff having been threatened with dispossession in the first part of Baisak, 1390 B.S. the plaintiff was :obliged to file the suit.
